Content:
The Explanation of the Yokai Puzzle is pretty blunt. Look at the corresponding pictures: The Carriage has two heads. "The Yokai of the Carriage had their heads removed" (2). The Umbrella has 4 arms. "The Yokai of the umbrella their arms." (4) The Kettle has 3 legs. "The Yokai of the Kettle their legs" (3). Now you take the numbers 2-4-3 and is this as the number of the object in the list of symbols. Carriage=2nd object / Umbrella=4th object / Kettle=3rd object. Thats why expecially the third symbol doesnt make any fuckin sense. But in Numbers it does.


all those fancy words and symbols are just smoke bombs. hope it helps for clarification.

Author: @onisensei443
Content: The pillars at the start are torii gates mark, In the Shinto faith they mark the path from the "Human World" to a "Sacred Place". In More recent media though they also represent gates to the spiritual world in general. The sealing talismans on them are......lets just say bad news. Sadly i think the Japanese setting is a huge part of why this gem is getting so much flak. Most of the settings that should be really ominous and alarming are lost on the rest of the world as they don't know the meaning and importance of a lot of it. The fox mask for example is really alarming as it could be really good or really bad depending on context as while there are benevolent "Zenko" messengers for Inari that were said to guide and protect...there were also malevolent "nogitsune" spirits that mislead and often killed wayward souls. So my guy should have been all kinds of worrying given the time....but most players wouldn't know that so it was lost, still a decently worrying moment of the game but probably not as thrilling as the devs had hoped. I feel like a lot of Silent Hill F is getting "Lost in Translation" kinda sucks honestly.

Author: @Hevensdragon
Content:
So a bit of folk lore, foxes are often attached to cases of spiriting away. The doctor is talking about about appeasing them at the start. The man with the fox mask is ether a onmyoji, or a fox spirit. It really depends on whos side he is on. If its a fox, then that makes the main character a foxes bride, he will act nice to her, but its to suduce, falling for him will be her death, if she is lucky. If its a onmyoji, basically a exorcist then he is probably her only hope, he also probably knows a lot about what is currently and going to happen. As reading the stars and knowing the future is a large part of onmyo.
The thing about the foxes, they can be both good or evil, the first omyoji, was born of a fox and its powers are what onmyoji all use down the line. They can be messengers of the gods. But they can also be great evils. Which is why they are treated with great care. You do not want to incur their wrath. 
Now I am leaning towards this being he is a fox not a onmyoji for a few reasons, but I am writing this early on in this vid. But I doubt we will find out this part. A onmyoji's actions may seem evil, they tend to know far more than they can say, as well as know that saying to much can change the desired course. They may also know about needed sacrifices. One big danger with anything based on Jap folk lore, the mental state matters, one can become a monster. So onmyoji are often very quite, giving very little info away, to avoid upsetting those they interact with. But this can make them very creepy, even when they are on your side. 
In large part this is because they were a very real thing history, onmyoji they were entire schools of con men, who claimed to practice magic.  They practiced being as mysterious as possible, to never reveal the fraud. 
Now if this will be a folk lore onmyoji or a real version, I would lean folk lore. 

That said I think its a fox, as that opens up all kind of messed up situations. She will probably end up with his child, and in that time period, a foxes child means she will be in all kinds of trouble and face a large amounts of persecution. As said above, if this route is the case, death would be a mercy, and its silent hill... so yeah this could get really dark.

Author: @weedcat1683
Content:
TL:DR Clunky controls made the game Scarier, Not old and redundant.

I am sad to see that these remakes took a more modernized aproach to the combat, The original games took advantage of the cluncky system. Your character always felt vulnerable during every strike. And the way that the character moved like a tank (Like most PS1 style games) made it feel so much more stressful to just run away as well. So you would basically feel like you were backed into a corner no matter what situation came at you.

Also a health bar is probably one of the most anti silent hill things ever, They used the heartrate monitor for the exact reason of leaving your current health ambiguous. You were never truely aware of just how close you were to being dead.

If you read all of this you'll notice something by now. The whole game was built around trying to make the player feel like the lacked proper control, And that was the point. By making the player have a distinct disconnect from their actions and the execution in game. You felt like every single encounter was an act of survival, Not just another obsticle that you had to clear out of your way.
